fieldworkDocument.title: Measgaichte / Miscellaneous
fieldworkDocument.note: [NOTES: in IPA transcriptions, the fieldworker uses [w] for [ɯ].]

item.description: Quot.: “dearg air a loch-bhlian dheas”, “dearg air a loch-bhlian cheàrr”. Note: the flank of sheep – used in marking.
Note: earmark.
Note: earmark.
Note: earmark.
Note: earmark confined, according to P.C., to one crofter in Marvig. The ear is folded lengthwise and a cut like a “gearradh-lùdaig” [q.v.] made, leaving a tongue in the middle of the ear.
Quot.: bàrr is tri rubaidh. Note: earmark. (Put also under rubadh.)
Note: earmark. (Also known as sgoltadh.)
[mȷɤ:ʴɫɑṉ] Note: earmark. [NOTES: the turned r used for the symbol which is unclear in the original.]
[su̜:ɫɑɡ] Note: earmark.
Note: earmark.
[kɾɛ̃:rũ̜n̪ɑx] Note: horse-mackerel.
Note: square frame on which fishing line is wound.
Note: (1) young lythe. (2) also applied to young, flighty girls.
Note: torsk (fish).
Note: spawn-pouch of the crab.
[bɔʴt̪iɑxk] Note: P.C.’s pronunciation of “muirtiachd”, a jellyfish. [NOTES: the turned r used for the symbol which is unclear in the original.]
Note: applied to a stinging jellyfish (adj.).
[sɡʹɤu̜ɫd̪əð] Note: long thin reddish jellyfish which stings. Buckie men called them “scalders”.
[ɡʹıbṉɔx] Note: a squid.
Note: starfish.
[bðɑɫɔx] Note: shellfish found in the sand. Has a spout which it can retract.
Note: a tidal wave, most noticeable in a shallow inlet. Doesn’t occur with every tide, or not noticeable. Often precedes bad weather.
[t̪u̜ɫu̜xɑṉ] Note: the part of the “mircean” nearer to the rock.
[bðiʃɡʹɑṉ] Note: edible root (silverweed?) found among potatoes.
Note: seaweed with bubbles on it.
[dʹe:ʃnʹɑɡ] Note: a small, thin “portan”, not as rounded in the back as the ordinary one. Not as blue.
Note: hermit crab.
[pɾɔ̃n̪ɔvw̃ɾɑx] Note: chewed “maorach” thrown out for bait to attract saithe.
Note: rope between the “cruaidh” at the end of a fishing line and the buoy.
[t̪ɔt̪ɑɫ] Quot.: “total fhaoileag”. Note: a flock of seagulls wheeling about near the surface of the sea where fish are.
Note: float perhaps 15 fathoms down tied to the “ceann” [q.v.] of the great-line or small line. Often made here of a circle of rope with corks on it right round. (Sometimes puta-sàs known as sàsair.)
Note: circle of cork floats strung together. Used as a “puta-sàs” (above).
Quot.: a’ sgràbadh. Note: working a grapnel. [Cf. sgràbair.]
Note: grapnel, for picking up lost fishing lines from the bottom. [Cf. sgràbadh.]
Quot.: am bàc. Note: the top rope from which a herring net is hung.
[ḏɑfəṉs] Note: small lengths of line attaching herring net to the “bàc” [q.v.].
Note: herring net with stones as weights.
[ɡʹe:vəl] Note: the ends of the herring net.
Note: the top corner of a herring net where the “géibheil” [q.v.] was attached to the “bàc” [q.v.].
[kɫɑɡən̪] Note: wooden top on a sheepskin buoy.
[sṯu̟ıə] Note: a kind of buoy made with a calf’s skin, the skin having been removed as whole as possible. The buoy had roughly the shape of the calf.
Note: spiked muzzle on a calf to prevent it suckling its mother.
Note: membrane, very thin covering.
[ıtʹıɑx] Note: gullet.
[sn̪ɑ̃:l] Note: anal passage.
[smĩɾkɑlʹɑx] Note: spinal marrow.
[lʹıɑvɔx] Note: applied to the colouring of a sheep’s face. Dirty white effect.
[sɡɾɔ̃ɡɑɡ] Note: small stump of a horn on a sheep.
[sɡɾɔ̃ɡɑx] Quot.: caora sgrogach. Note: sheep with small stumps of horns.
Quot.: caora le adhaircean chros. Note: sheep with horns curving in towards the face.
Quot.: caora le adhaircean sgaoilt. Note: a sheep with wide horns.
[ʃeðəmiɡʹə] Note: a ram in such poor condition that he’s not allowed near sheep.
[ru̟ɡʹə] Note: [a ram which] has only one testicle in the sac. The other one up in its back (acc. to P.C.).
[ʃeðeɡʹ] Note: a sheep in poor condition and because of some deficiency won’t fatten. (Pine in English.)
Note: black-leg.
Quot.: “na gonaidhean”. Note: growths in the mouths of cattle which prevented them from eating properly. Usually cut with shears.
Note: used here for bitch. “Saidh” not used.
[bu̟idʹ] Note: puffin.
[ɑ̃ṉd̪u̟] Note: guillemot.
[ɑlɑṉbɔd̪ˈɑə] Note: a sea-bird which forces seagulls to disgorge its [sic] food, and swallows it itself. Probably the skua.
Quot.: “Tha’n fhairge na glinn.” “Ann an glinn na mara.” Note: Referring to troughs in a heavy swell.
[kɫɑɡən̪] Quot.: “Claigionn na Càbaig”. Note: Referring to the extremity of Kebock Head.
Note: butterfly.
[kɑʃɑṉkũ̟ɑx] Quot.: “Caisean-cumhach na Bealltainn”. Note: spell of bad weather at the beginning of May.
Quot.: “na faoilich”. Note: spell of cold winds in January and into February.
[t̪ɑ̃ṉiʃɡʹ] Note: spectre in the form of a person.
[t̪ɑ:vɔɾəɣ] Note: ghostly resemblance of a person, usually connected with a future happening.
[rɛ̃ṉɔx] Note: bracken. (Pronunciation.)
[ɡðibɔṉ] Note: applied to a person, usually a boy, who is not as developed as he should be physically at his age.
[pɾɔhɑʃtʹɑx] Quot.: “prothaisteach de bhalach”. Note: well-built young lad.
[sɡʹel] Quot.: “Tha sgeil uamhasach air an te sin.” Note: She has an awful lot to say.
[fɑɾɑvɑlʹtʹɑx] Quot.: “’S e boirionnach farbhailteach a th’innt.” Note: used of a person who makes a welcoming fuss when a person goes into her house.
[ʃurəðɑxk] Quot.: “Tha thu ann a’ sin a’ siurraireachd nan tighean fad an latha.” Note: used of a woman who is always in and out of houses.
[ʃu̜rɑɡ] Note: a woman who is always in and out of houses.
Quot.: “Bha mi aimsirean [ɑmɑʃəðəṉ] mas do chuimhnich mi air.” Note: I took ages before I remembered it.
Note: a light cuff or clip.
[kɫɑ̃ĩɾɑxk] Quot.: “cearc a’ claimhreachd as a’ ghainmich”. Note: used of a hen sgrabbling [sic] in sand.
Note: liquid fat floating, e.g. on the surface of soup.
